tagline: A twelve-mile loop through the old Pee Dee rice country.
intro: Choppee Road leaves US 701 and runs southeast a little over two miles to Plantersville Road, which turns northeast and carries on about ten miles back to 701. The loop keeps near the Great Pee Dee River, among the plantations and rice fields of a culture that flourished here from about 1750 to about 1910.

Plantersville itself is a community on 701, six miles north of Georgetown. Samworth Plantation, now a state Department of Natural Resources property, is kept for watching wildlife and learning about its habitat.

moments.title: Prince Frederick's Chapel Ruins
moments.text: Only the front wall and tower remain of a Gothic Revival church begun for the rice planters in 1859, finished in 1876 and pulled down as unsafe in 1966.

moments.title: Chicora Wood Plantation
moments.text: An 1819 house and rice mill on the north side of the road, where 630 enslaved people worked by 1860 and Elizabeth Allston Pringle later ran the place and wrote A Woman Rice Planter.
